parsed.why: Enforced same-sex criminalisation with recent imprisonment, routine police extortion and prolonged LGBTQI detentions, forced anal examinations as torture-level evidence, mob violence including officers, near-zero public acceptance and no protection policy.

Little documented street hostility; friction is institutional — onsen segregation, family-register custody, ward-office document refusals. Top-court bathroom and detention rulings protect trans people, but no anti-discrimination statute and uneven practice below the courts.

Decriminalised conduct, functioning rule of law, no documented police or violence targeting of trans people; but no gender recognition, frontier document mismatch, discrimination grounds omit identity, gay culture invisible — thin record, no acceptance evidence.

Working protections: anti-discrimination law covering services, hate-crime prosecutions, supreme-court safeguards for detained trans foreigners, sterilisation ban. Offset by official transphobia at head-of-state level, survey-measured harassment concentrated among trans respondents, unresolved prison placement.

No criminalisation, but no recognition, no anti-discrimination or hate-crime framework, no functioning recourse, hostile-climate assessment, concealment norm, activist's unconfirmed 2019 killing and dated camp harassment; thin record extrapolates from absent protections.
